items.followUp: How does meiosis help maintain chromosome number and produce variation?

rubric.why: Meiosis halves the chromosome number in gametes, so fertilisation restores the usual number and maintains it across generations.
rubric.description: Explains how meiosis helps maintain the chromosome number across generations.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that meiosis halves the chromosome number in gametes or that it maintains the chromosome number after fertilisation.

rubric.why: Meiosis produces genetic variation, including through crossing over and independent assortment.
rubric.description: States that meiosis produces genetic variation or names a process that produces it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for genetic variation, crossing over, or independent assortment.

modelAnswer: Meiosis halves the chromosome number in gametes, maintaining the chromosome number of a species after fertilisation.
It produces genetic variation through crossing over and independent assortment.

items.followUp: Why do prokaryotes reproduce without meiosis?

rubric.why: Prokaryotes lack a true nucleus, unlike the cells in which meiosis takes place.
rubric.description: States that prokaryotes do not have a true nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the absence of a true nucleus.

rubric.why: Meiosis involves pairing and separation of homologous chromosomes, which prokaryotes lack.
rubric.description: Explains that prokaryotes lack the homologous chromosome pairs needed for meiosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that prokaryotes lack homologous chromosome pairs.

modelAnswer: They lack homologous chromosome pairs, which are needed for meiosis.
